# Analects — received Chinese text and James Legge translation

The selected carrier is Chinese Text Project's Zi Lu chapter, accessed 8 September 2026, with received Chinese and English attributed to James Legge. Complete 13.3 and 13.15 were read in both columns. These are speeches represented within a received work; no composition date or verbatim historical utterance is inferred from the named speakers. The setting in 13.3 is Zilu's question about governing Wei. That textual setting is secure within the selected passage; identifying a specific accession dispute or dating the speech requires separate historical evidence.

A supplementary [METIS/ETH transcription](https://metis.ethz.ch/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/The-Analects_Confucius_EnglishLegge.pdf), saved at `working/sources-texts-references/primary-texts/chinese-zhengming/analects-legge-ethz.pdf`, carries the same selected English passages on printed pp.49 and 51 (PDF indices 49 and 51). Its opening page labels the work Analects but also prints “Laozi” and identifies Legge as “Oxford: 1867.” Those conflicting metadata are not adopted as the selected print edition. No full-work reading, manuscript collation or critical-edition verification is claimed.

<a id="passages"></a>
## Received primary passages

<a id="analects-ctext-legge-q001"></a>
### q001 — 13.3: names, speech and the consequences of government

**Paraphrase:** Asked what should come first in governing Wei, the Master proposes rectifying names. Zilu objects to its apparent impracticality. The reply first requires restraint where knowledge is lacking, then follows a consequential sequence: defective naming disorders speech, obstructs affairs, prevents rites and music from flourishing, misdirects punishments and leaves people unable to act. It ends by requiring names that can be spoken appropriately and speech that can be put into practice.

**Locator:** Analects 13.3, entire exchange, from Zilu's question through the final requirement concerning speech; Chinese Text Project, Zi Lu §3. Supplementary English transcription: METIS printed p.49.

**Verification:** saved Chinese and English columns read 2026-09-08; complete selected passage also read in the ETH-hosted English transcription. Legge's rendering of 言不順 elaborates the relation to truth; that English phrasing is not an independent Chinese lexical definition. The passage is a normative political argument involving ritual and punishment, not an observed test of government or a universal theory of classification. Trust is an E4 operational consequence developed from accountable speech and action, not a translation of a trust term in this passage.

<a id="analects-ctext-legge-q002"></a>
### q002 — 13.15: rule without contradiction

**Paraphrase:** Duke Ding asks whether one saying can make a state prosper or perish. The response resists such immediate causal compression and distinguishes recognising the difficulty of rule from delighting in never being contradicted. Unopposed good counsel and unopposed bad counsel have different consequences; the latter exposes a danger to the state.

**Locator:** Analects 13.15, entire two-part exchange; Chinese Text Project, Zi Lu §15; supplementary METIS printed p.51.

**Verification:** complete Chinese and English passage read 2026-09-08. This is a textual warning about rule and counsel, not evidence of an instituted right of dissent, equal participation or a modern revision procedure. Its conditional distinction survives those limits.

These passages **source** the Chinese comparison in [E4's Account operation](../../../../etymologies/symbol-account-and-trust/WHOLE-FIELD.md#account-does-not-replace-source). The warning about unopposed bad counsel **compares** with [C27's protected criterion](../../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C27-Protected-Account-Occupied-Zero-Source-Claim.md); the difference between represented political counsel and Taylor's native QL operation remains explicit. The [Ministry dictionary](../../../classical-philology/ministry-of-education-taiwan/moe-2021-revised-mandarin-dictionary/moe-2021-revised-mandarin-dictionary.md#moe-2021-revised-mandarin-dictionary-q001) **defines** the selected lexical use without establishing a common root or a single continuous Chinese institutional practice.
